Greetings from middle England Voat! My name is Mark L Noyce and I'm an independent author who just released my latest book "Immortal Space" and am here to host an AMA for two reasons.

  1. It'll be fun.

  2. Promotion. At least I'm honest.

Here's the description of Immortal Space from Amazon;

The year is 2520. Trent Saxon is returning home to Earth from a self imposed isolation in space. He's shot down not long after entering the Milky Way. His ship makes it to the blue planet but his life is lost in the process.

Geoff Avery is guarding the morgue as he does most nights when he hears a sound. He pushes aside his fear and finds Trent alive and well. Geoff quickly learns Trent isn't the someone who will die that easily as he makes a bold claim about his age. A few experiments later and Geoff is convinced.

Follow Trent and Geoff as they embark on an adventure traversing two planets, make friends and enemies, and form a bond that can last several lifetimes as they learn about the past, present and future. Both of the world and of themselves. Why can't Trent die? Was the attack really random? And just what's with that scar on his chest?

Here are a few topics you can ask me about to help get things going.

  1. I'm English. Ask me anything about England, my thoughts on things in England. Europe, anything like that.

  2. I'm a writer, self published at that. Ask me anything about the writing or self publishing process.

  3. I've been blogging for the past few years so you can ask me anything about that too.

  4. I'm also a volunteer at my local charity shop so I'll be happy to take any questions on that.

  5. I've lived with a depression a lot of my life. I was even sent to a child psychologist at 14 and was put on sleeping pills and anti-depressents. Neither worked.

  6. I'm also a wrestling fan and co-host a podcast on it every week. You can ask me about that but my knowledge will be limited because I'm just a guy who speaks in a mic. Another guy takes care of all the complicated technical stuff.

  7. Just anything in general! Go wild. The more random and weird the question the more random and weird my answer can be, no?

In preparation for this AMA, and in honour of my latest release, all my short stories are currently free to download on Amazon. They can be found directly from my author page on Amazon, which is also where you can find Immortal Space. This deal is only for today and tomorrow.

You can find me on Twitter here, and my blog The Rambling Person is here. I'll be answering questions for as long as I can really. If I don't answer a question today I'll answer it when I wake up tomorrow. I sent messages to /u/Smite before putting this post up so hopefully Smite will be around soon to verify me. If not then I'll happy send to them everything I sent to Smite so they can do the verifying.
I Am Mark L Noyce, Independent Author and Blogger from England Who Just Released My Latest Book. AMA!
How hard is the Sci Fi in this new book? Would you say it's more science than fiction or vice versa?
Hmm. I've never thought about that. One particular section is very science heavy but outside of that it's more fiction than science.
Thanks, it looks interesting enough to give a go. I'll slot it into my reading queue. Cheers.

Podcast questions: - How often do you publish a new show? - What do you use to record (phone, computer, etc.)?

Writing question: - How often do you write (hours per day, days per week, etc.)?

Podcast; It's a weekly show. We record every Sunday from 2PM EST to 4PM EST. The few times we have a guest on the show they're impressed I'm doing a podcast halfway around the world (It's based in the US and I'm the only person not in North America). The podcast is essentially a Skype call that the main host records. He has a proper studio setup and all the other guys have professional microphones. I use my headset mic and it's good enough for that at least. Sometimes one of the guys actually calls us from his Xbox One.

Writing; It depends really. On average I can write about 6-8 thousand words a week spread across three days. That was the pace I was going with one story. People don't realise how mentally taxing, and even physically taxing, writing can be. It doesn't sound like much to sit and type for a few hours but it can be a bitch. Especially mentally. Nothing kills you inside like continuous writing.

I've always wondered how long it takes authors to write... how long does it take for you? The average length to write, say, 100 pages? What's the best/worst part of the writing process?

Thanks for the ama!

You're welcome. I can only speak for myself but I have a fast typing speed. The only problem is I can't maintain it for very long. I can write about 2000 words (four pages-ish) in about 2 hours on a good day. Faster if I enjoy what I write and slower if I don't. So 100 pages...50 hours. That's about 10 weeks or so. That's when typing too. I write faster a full page faster with a pen but it's less words because my handwriting is larger than 11 point font apparently.

The best part of the writing process is that it can be a lot of fun. I enjoy creating new worlds and characters and having them explore and interact. The worst part is that it's a lot more demanding than people would think. I have no idea how people like Stephen King write as much as they do.

As someone who has tried to write a book but utterly failed... yes I agree in that it is very demanding. Sometimes exhausting, even. So much respect to you!

Do you do this as a full time job? Which is your main pursuit, blogging or writing?

I'm unemployed so this is the closest I have to a job but I've never made much money. Self publishing is very self reliant and I don't have the money to really run advertising campaigns or even to pay a literary agent to set things up for me. I plucked up the courage to approach a radio station but they haven't replied to me yet. It's something I hope to eventually turn into something that is financially viable.

I dedicate far more time to writing than to blogging. Blogging came first though. I was encouraged to write fiction through the people who read the nonfiction of my blog.
